body_markdown:
News


September 1, 2026


Amber Wesdorp


**DENVER, September 1, 2026** Quantum Space, a company developing the next generation of advanced maneuverable spacecraft for national security and commercial operations, has selected Quindar’s autonomous mission management service to support operations for its Scout and Ranger spacecraft missions.


Through this collaboration, Quantum Space has immediate access to Quindar’s cloud-native secure software which has been integrated on more than 400 commercial antennas to support missions across a range of orbital regimes.


“Quantum Space’s spacecraft are being designed to operate dynamically across the orbits most critical to U.S. national security. Quindar provides a flexible mission management solution for our missions and scales with our fleet, allowing our team to remain focused on delivering greater maneuverability and mission flexibility.”- Philip Bracken, Chief Technology Officer.


**Scaling from Prime** **Mission** **to Fleet Operations**


Quantum Space is preparing its Prime mission for launch the summer of 2027. The mission is expected to demonstrate spacecraft performance, payload hosting, data collection, maneuvering, and rendezvous and proximity operations.


Quindar’s automation-first workflows will help Quantum Space manage spacecraft, payloads, ground assets, and mission users as the company scales and advances Scout and Ranger missions. Quindar’s software is designed to support secure deployment and mission-specific workflows while reducing the time and complexity typically associated with building bespoke ground systems.


“Government space programs should not have to choose between moving quickly and building secure, resilient operations. Quantum Space is developing a highly capable spacecraft platform for complex defense missions. Quindar provides the secure mission management infrastructure needed to bring those missions into operations faster and scale them with confidence.” – Nate Hamet, CEO and Co-Founder of Quindar


The partnership comes as Quantum Space expands its U.S. manufacturing base with a new facility in Tulsa, Oklahoma while expanding operations in California and Maryland. Quindar’s cloud-native architecture supports this distributed model by providing authorized teams access to a consistent operational environment from approved locations. Engineering, integration, mission planning, and operations personnel can work from the same mission information without relying on a single physical control room or maintaining separate software environments at every facility.


**About Quantum Space**


‍Quantum Space is building the next generation of advanced maneuverable spacecraft for national security, civil, and commercial space operations. Its highly maneuverable spacecraft are beingdesigned to address the needs of national security and commercial operators. With patented propulsion, extended on-orbit endurance, and modular flexibility, these platforms are being engineered to outmaneuver legacy satellites and operate dynamically across diverse mission sets. For more information, visit www.quantumspaceinc.com.


**About Quindar**


Quindar is a mission management service for modern space operations. Its five integrated products – Portal, Event, Control, Plan, and Flight – provide mission teams with a common operating picture across spacecraft, payloads, ground networks, and operational stakeholders. Built for commercial, civil, and national security missions, Quindar delivers secure, resilient, and automation-first operations through cloud-based or on-premises deployments. For more information, visit www.quindar.space.
